faqs.question: How many credit hours do I need for federal student loans?
faqs.answer: Graduate students must be enrolled at least half-time, which is 5 graduate credit hours in a fall or spring term, to receive federal student loans.

faqs.question: When should I file the FAFSA?
faqs.answer: File the FAFSA as soon as it opens on October 1 for the following academic year. The priority deadline for institutional aid is March 15.

faqs.question: What happens to my aid if I drop below half-time?
faqs.answer: Dropping below half-time can cancel loan disbursements for the term and start the six-month grace period on existing loans. Talk to the financial aid office before dropping courses.

faqs.question: Do graduate assistantships affect my financial aid?
faqs.answer: Yes. Assistantship tuition waivers and stipends count as resources and can reduce the amount of loans you are offered. Report a new assistantship to the financial aid office within 10 days.

faqs.question: How do I appeal a satisfactory academic progress suspension?
faqs.answer: Submit the SAP appeal form with a personal statement and an academic plan signed by your advisor. Appeals are reviewed within 15 business days of submission, and the decision is sent to your university e-mail.

faqs.question: How can I contact the financial aid office?
faqs.answer: E-mail finaid@example.edu or call (555) 010-0142, Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Include your student ID number in e-mails, never your full social security number.
